speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing shortness of breath and increased abdominal girth; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you've noticed any changes in your bowel or urinary habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has this abdominal enlargement become so significant that you are having trouble breathing even when resting, or does the shortness of breath only occur during exertion? Also, have you noticed any pain in your pelvis or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma (Meigs' Syndrome). The combination of a large ovarian mass, ascites (increased abdominal girth), and pleural effusion causing shortness of breath in a nulliparous woman is classic for this benign condition, even with the presence of fatigue. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound, Chest X-Ray.
